works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.description: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War, one of the most translated works in history.

translations.previewText: Achilles' baneful wrath resound, O Goddess, that imposed / Infinite sorrows on the Greeks, and many brave souls loosed / From breasts heroic—sent them far to that invisible cave / That no light comforts; and their limbs to dogs and vultures gave.
Achilles' wrath, to Greece the direful spring / Of woes unnumber'd, heavenly goddess, sing! / That wrath which hurl'd to Pluto's gloomy reign / The souls of mighty chiefs untimely slain.
Sing, heav'nly Muse, the fatal wrath of Peleus' son Achilles; / Wrath which to Greece unnumber'd evils brought; / Full many a stalwart hero's soul it sent / Far down to Hades' realm.
Sing, goddess, the anger of Peleus' son Achilleus / and its devastation, which put pains thousandfold upon the Achaians, / hurled in their multitudes to the house of Hades strong souls / of heroes.
Rage—Goddess, sing the rage of Peleus' son Achilles, / murderous, doomed, that cost the Achaeans countless losses, / hurling down to the House of Death so many sturdy souls.
The rage of Achilles—sing it now, goddess, sing through me / the deadly rage that caused the Achaeans such grief / and hurled down to Hades the souls of so many fighters.

works.title: Les Fleurs du Mal
works.author: Charles Baudelaire
works.description: Baudelaire's landmark collection exploring beauty, decadence, and the modern city.

translations.previewText: When the low heavy sky weighs like a lid / On the groaning spirit, prey to long ennui, / And from the horizon's rim to the extreme / Of heaven's blue, a dark day seems to flee.

translations.translator: George Dillon & Edna St. Vincent Millay
translations.previewText: When skies are low and heavy as a lid / Over the mind tormented by disgust, / And, circling in the light of a dim day, / Darkness pours down upon us, thick as dust.
When skies are low and heavy as a lid on the groaning spirit / helpless under long ennui, / and from the rim of the grey horizon / black daylight drizzles down on us, sadder than any night.
When skies are low and heavy as a lid / pressed down by gloom upon the groaning mind, / when all the horizon's circuit, black and livid, / pours on us daylight darker than the night.

works.title: Masnavi-ye Ma'navi
works.author: Jalāl ad-Dīn Rūmī
works.description: Rumi's magnum opus, six books of Persian verse exploring mysticism and the soul's longing.

translations.previewText: Listen to the reed, how a tale it telleth; / How it singeth of separations! / 'Twixt the time when from the reed-bed torn I was, / Man and woman have to my piping mourned.
Hearken to this Reed how it tells a tale, complaining of separations—'Ever since I was parted from the reed-bed, my lament hath caused man and woman to moan.'
Listen to the reed and the tale it tells, / how it sings of separation: / 'Ever since they tore me from my reed bed, / my wail has caused men and women to weep.'
Listen to this reed how it tells a story, / how it sings of separation. / Since I was cut from the reed bed, / I have made this crying sound.

Hear this reed—how it composes tales of separation's pain, / of how from the reed bed they tore it—how it made the air complain: / since the day they cut me from the reed bed, men and women moan / to my reed-cry.

works.title: Veinte poemas de amor y una canción desesperada
works.author: Pablo Neruda
works.description: Neruda's passionate early collection, one of the most widely translated poetry books in the world.

translations.previewText: I want to do with you what spring does with the cherry trees. / Tonight I can write the saddest lines. / I loved her, and sometimes she loved me too.
I can write the saddest poem of all tonight. / Write, for instance: 'The night is full of stars, / and the stars, blue, shiver in the distance.' / The night wind turns in the sky and sings.
I want to do with you what spring does to the cherry trees. / Tonight I can write the saddest lines. I loved her, and sometimes she loved me too.

works.title: Duineser Elegien
works.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
works.description: Rilke's visionary elegies on beauty, angels, and what it means to be human.

translations.previewText: Who, if I cried out, would hear me among the angels' hierarchies? / and even if one of them suddenly pressed me against his heart, / I should fade in the strength of his stronger existence.
Who, if I cried out, would hear me among the angels' orders? / And even if one of them suddenly pressed me against his heart, / I would fade in the strength of his stronger existence.
Who, if I cried out, would hear me among the orders of angels? / And even if one of them suddenly took me to his heart: / I'd be consumed by his stronger existence.
